description: Fictional example quest library for REGEN offline concept demo. Completion does not imply verified outcomes.

quests.title: Find your first spark
quests.summary: Choose one community challenge and one strength you bring.
quests.objective: A privately identified concern and useful strength.
steps: Think of one thing that helps people or nature thrive where you live.
Write down one frustration you would like to see improved.
Identify one strength, curiosity, or accessible way you could contribute.
quests.reflection_prompt: What feels small enough to try this week?
quests.accessibility_alternative: You can think or record a voice note rather than write.
quests.consent_requirement: No permission needed; keep reflection private.
quests.safety_notes: Do not document or diagnose other people.

quests.title: Spot three existing strengths
quests.summary: Notice resources already helping a place function.
steps: Observe your area from a safe public place, a community bulletin, or public websites.
Identify three existing strengths such as a library, mutual-aid resource, or accessible meeting place.
Consider who might be excluded and one question worth exploring.
quests.reflection_prompt: Which existing strength could be supported rather than replaced?
quests.accessibility_alternative: Complete entirely online using public resources.
quests.consent_requirement: Publicly available information only; no contacting anyone required.
quests.safety_notes: Do not photograph residents, residences, or private activity.

quests.title: Explore a skill pathway
quests.summary: Pick a skill you can practice without expensive equipment.
quests.objective: One selected skill and a first practice step.
steps: Review the eight skill domains.
Choose one interest and a small first practice action.
Name a no-cost or low-cost resource you could use.
quests.reflection_prompt: What would make this activity easier to access?
quests.accessibility_alternative: Use spoken reflection, translation, or a partner.
quests.consent_requirement: No special permission; respect local rules and others' privacy.
quests.safety_notes: Do not collect identifying information about others.

quests.title: Repair before replacing
quests.summary: Investigate one safe repair or reuse opportunity.
quests.objective: A safe decision about whether to repair, donate, reuse, or replace.
steps: Choose one non-hazardous household item.
Find a credible repair or reuse option and note estimated effort and cost.
If safe and within your skills, take a small step—or record the best option for later.
quests.reflection_prompt: Did the repair option save a resource or reveal a barrier?
quests.accessibility_alternative: Do the research from home; no physical repair is required.
quests.consent_requirement: Obtain permission before touching anything that belongs to someone else.
quests.safety_notes: Avoid electricity, batteries, chemicals, structural repairs, and other hazardous work without a qualified professional.

quests.title: Learn where food waste begins
quests.summary: Identify one avoidable waste source without compromising food safety.
quests.objective: One plausible waste source and one safety constraint.
steps: Review a reliable local public resource about food waste.
Distinguish edible surplus, unavoidable scraps, and items that must be discarded for safety.
Pick one low-risk prevention idea worth investigating.
quests.reflection_prompt: What should never be reused or donated for safety reasons?
quests.accessibility_alternative: Read or listen to information without observing a workplace.
quests.consent_requirement: No special permission; respect local rules and others' privacy.
quests.safety_notes: Do not collect identifying information about others.

quests.title: Notice an accessibility barrier
quests.summary: Identify a friction point and propose a respectful improvement.
quests.objective: An accessibility suggestion without identifying people.
steps: Choose a public service or website that you already use.
Notice one step that might create access friction; do not assume one person represents everyone.
Draft a constructive, privately held suggestion with an alternate approach.
quests.reflection_prompt: Who should be asked before a solution is adopted?
quests.consent_requirement: If you later share feedback, use an official channel and respect participants' consent.
quests.safety_notes: Never photograph or publicly identify disabled individuals or private medical details.

quests.title: Observe food waste respectfully
quests.summary: Create a tiny, anonymous baseline with permission.
quests.objective: A non-sensitive baseline for one location and period.
steps: Ask the household or organization for permission and define the observation scope.
Choose one safe aggregate measure: portions, approximate mass, or count over a defined period.
Record only totals; note conditions that could change the interpretation.
quests.reflection_prompt: What cannot be concluded from this observation?
quests.accessibility_alternative: Observe your own household or use a published anonymous dataset.
quests.consent_requirement: Explicit permission required in a workplace or group setting.
quests.safety_notes: Do not record customer, worker, or household identities; follow food-handling rules.

quests.title: Make a public resource easier to understand
quests.summary: Summarize a verified resource in clear, neutral language.
quests.objective: An accurate draft summary linked to its public source.
steps: Select one existing public service page or program you find useful.
Make a short plain-language summary and link the original information.
Check the summary against the source, including eligibility, limits, and dates.
quests.reflection_prompt: What might someone misunderstand if the source were not linked?
quests.accessibility_alternative: Audio summaries and multilingual versions are welcome.
quests.consent_requirement: Share only if allowed under applicable rights and local rules.
quests.safety_notes: Avoid personal data, unauthorized legal advice, and partisan misrepresentation.

quests.title: Host a consent-based repair exchange
quests.summary: Create a small collaborative learning session.
quests.objective: One planned, safe repair-and-reuse exchange with clear roles.
steps: Invite participants without pressure and choose a permitted, accessible venue.
Define a narrow, nonhazardous item category and safety roles.
Discuss lessons, accessibility, and whether further sessions are wanted.
quests.reflection_prompt: Did everyone benefit and have a meaningful choice?
quests.accessibility_alternative: Coordinate a remote repair-resource exchange instead.
quests.consent_requirement: Participants and venue must opt in; receive permission for any photos.
quests.safety_notes: No electrical, high-risk, or regulated repairs; obtain qualified supervision where needed.

quests.title: Test a safe waste-prevention idea
quests.summary: Try one reversible change with participating stakeholders.
quests.objective: A documented pilot plan with a before/after comparison.
steps: Get explicit authorization and invite affected staff into planning.
Choose a food-safety-preserving, reversible prevention change and define success and failure criteria.
Use anonymous totals to compare against the baseline and ask whether labor burdens changed.
quests.reflection_prompt: What benefits, hidden costs, and uncertainties did the pilot reveal?
quests.accessibility_alternative: Design a hypothetical pilot using example numbers instead of operating one.
quests.consent_requirement: Participating site and impacted workers must consent; authorized food-safety review required.
quests.safety_notes: Do not bypass food handling policy, sanitation rules, labor protections, or regulatory reporting.

quests.title: Translate a civic meeting into a learning note
quests.summary: Help people follow a public decision without partisan framing.
steps: Find an official agenda, minutes, or public recording.
Identify the decision, public-comment rules, timing, and how to read primary sources.
Invite correction and publish only if the source is public and the summary is accurate.
quests.reflection_prompt: How can someone with an opposing view confirm the same facts?
quests.accessibility_alternative: Work asynchronously with an accessible transcript if available.
quests.consent_requirement: No permission required to summarize public governmental materials where lawful.
quests.safety_notes: Do not profile attendees, target officials, or selectively misrepresent statements.

quests.title: Sketch a voluntary change compact
quests.summary: Draft accountable milestones for an institution that opts in.
quests.objective: A draft compact with affected-party review and verifiable milestones.
steps: Identify a voluntary partner organization and the people affected by the proposed change.
Describe the problem, baseline, non-negotiable safety protections, resources, and fair transition support.
Define independent review, milestones, consent, grievance processes, and lawful escalation options.
quests.reflection_prompt: What would demonstrate real repair rather than reputation management?
quests.accessibility_alternative: Create a simulated compact with fictional names, clearly labeled as a simulation.
quests.consent_requirement: Real organizational participation, worker input, and any publication require explicit consent and appropriate governance.
quests.safety_notes: No covert infiltration, private information gathering, shaming campaigns, or replacing regulatory obligations.
